scope: Interpretation and localization of the frozen 602 CTA records; no classification changes.

gap_groups.label: Duplicated regulatory and antigen-related families
gap_groups.rationale: Family annotations and developmental RNA explain their inclusion. Exact-copy human function is largely uncharacterized.

gap_groups.label: Germ-cell structure and chromatin
gap_groups.rationale: Mouse sperm or testis studies provide biological leads; they do not establish the exact human protein.

gap_groups.label: Reproductive secretory families
gap_groups.rationale: Defensin, lipocalin and spermadhesin families. Human secretion is annotated for DEFB113 and LCN9; SPADH localization is unresolved.

gap_groups.label: Maternal / oocyte-associated proteins
gap_groups.rationale: Oocyte-associated RNA and, for PABPN1L, mouse maternal-to-zygotic transition experiments.

gap_groups.label: Other poorly characterized reproductive proteins
gap_groups.rationale: Measured reproductive association and coding annotations supply the main support; family names do not establish tumor specificity.

gap_groups.label: Sensory channel
gap_groups.rationale: Mouse taste physiology identifies a normal-function question. The human taste-cell compartment remains to be resolved.

gap_groups.label: Unnamed loci and a readthrough
gap_groups.rationale: Six unnamed coding loci and the ATF7-NPFF readthrough. Lack of a stable name or a dedicated experiment does not negate a qualifying coding reference.

concern_groups.label: Direct adult normal-tissue protein
concern_groups.next_action: Adjudicate the tissue and cell findings against the normal-expression policy.

concern_groups.label: Physiological state or producing compartment
concern_groups.next_action: Identify the expressing normal cell, physiological state and relevant protection tier.

concern_groups.label: Normal RNA / function requires localization
concern_groups.next_action: Resolve native human producing cells, protein abundance and assay specificity.

concern_groups.label: Normal assay cannot separate related copies
concern_groups.next_action: Resolve the exact copy or proteoform before assigning a member-specific exclusion.

concern_groups.label: Plasma affinity-assay association
concern_groups.next_action: Verify the measured molecule, reagent specificity and normal source tissue.

concern_groups.label: Unnamed locus; little characterization
concern_groups.next_action: Keep the qualifying coding record; do not borrow a named paralog’s papers. Experimental characterization is a priority, not a new admission requirement.

concern_groups.label: Shared protein annotation
concern_groups.next_action: Map the observed protein sequence to the selected locus before transferring experiments.

concern_groups.label: Readthrough-specific evidence missing
concern_groups.next_action: Verify junction-spanning RNA and the selected product; parent-gene experiments do not establish the readthrough.

concern_groups.label: Experimental challenge to protein-coding status
concern_groups.next_action: Reconcile the noncoding interpretation with the selected reference translation.

concern_groups.label: Proteoform attribution
concern_groups.next_action: Assign measurements to GALP or alarin and their specific sequences.

concern_groups.label: RNA without selective protein detection
concern_groups.next_action: Reconcile the tested samples and assay sensitivity with older cross-reactive protein claims.

concerns.observation: Plasma protein-affinity / pQTL associations nominate MANSC4.
concerns.next_action: Verify the reagent’s target and the producing tissue; a plasma association is not tissue-localized protein evidence.
concerns.evidence_details: Plasma proteomic/pQTL studies associate the assay labelled MANSC4 with type-1 diabetes outcomes and, separately, normal-tension glaucoma. The glaucoma study combines UK Biobank Olink protein measurements with several pQTL cohorts and Mendelian-randomization analyses.
concerns.interpretation: A plasma affinity signal and genetic association do not localize normal protein to a tissue. Genetic effects can concern protein abundance or assay binding. Verify reagent selectivity and use an orthogonal peptide assay before treating the signal as identified circulating MANSC4 or assigning a producing cell.

concerns.observation: Recent work supports a nucleolar long-noncoding-RNA interpretation of the FRG2 family and challenges translation claims.
concerns.next_action: Review the exact locus and reading frame against the published experiments before retaining a protein-level claim.
concerns.evidence_details: The 2025 study introduced N- or C-terminal FLAG tags into predicted FRG2-family ORFs in HeLa and HEK293 cells. Tagged transcripts were detected and induced by doxorubicin, but FLAG immunoblots did not detect protein. Ribosome-profile and proteomic searches, including a HeLa experiment detecting more than 6,000 proteins, also found no FRG2 protein. RNA experiments support nucleolar/chromatin functions.
concerns.interpretation: This is affirmative experimental counterevidence to a protein interpretation, stronger than simply lacking a paper. The work examines several paralogs and edited bulk cell populations; align its tested transcripts/frames to the selected FRG2 or FRG2B sequence. Failure in those models is not a universal demonstration that no condition produces a protein.

concerns.observation: Qualifying reference coding sequence and measured RNA; no exact-locus protein experiment was verified.
concerns.next_action: Retain as a discovery candidate under the existing translation rule; improve sequence-linked annotation and characterization.
concerns.evidence_details: The released record has a qualifying annotated coding sequence and measured RNA supporting its admission route. The recorded literature searches did not verify an exact-locus protein experiment.
concerns.interpretation: An unnamed locus is poorly characterized, not experimentally shown to be noncoding. The existing rule accepts a qualifying reference CDS, so the absence of an experimental protein paper does not itself revoke CTA admission. Sequence-linked translation and function remain discovery work.

concerns.observation: Normal lactating breast expression; tumor antibody-blockade studies also identify a cell-surface target.
concerns.next_action: Retain lactation and mammary-cell context in the normal-expression decision.
concerns.evidence_details: BTN1A1 is a component of the milk-fat-globule membrane and is expressed by normal lactating mammary epithelium. The tumor study separately investigates cell-surface BTN1A1 and antibody blockade.
concerns.interpretation: Lactation is a normal physiological state that a resting adult-tissue panel can underrepresent. A tumor-surface observation does not establish cancer specificity. The normal decision must name lactating mammary cells rather than treating milk protein as evidence of no adult expression.

concerns.observation: Reagent-discriminated protein findings include normal donor serum and fetal / placental contexts.
concerns.next_action: Identify the adult producing tissue; serum detection alone does not locate the source cell.
concerns.evidence_details: Recent monoclonal-antibody studies distinguish CRIPTO3 from the closely related CRIPTO1. They report protein in normal donor serum as well as tumor samples. A separate study maps CRIPTO3 in human placenta, umbilical cord and multiple fetal tissues.
concerns.interpretation: The fetal and placental findings support an oncofetal association. Normal adult serum establishes extracellular detection but does not identify the adult source cell, secretion route or a tumor-cell surface epitope. Those are separate questions.

concerns.observation: Human hair-cuticle RNA and protein findings.
concerns.next_action: Distinguish mature hair from living follicular and regenerative cells.
concerns.evidence_details: The human KAP24.1 study combines in-situ hybridization and antibody microscopy, locating expression in the middle/upper hair cuticle. The HPA extended hair panel also reports cuticle staining.
concerns.interpretation: The finding is anatomically restricted. Mature hair is keratinized material, while its production involves differentiating follicular cells. Neither a blanket skin exclusion nor a blanket disposable-hair allowance follows without specifying the living cells recognized.

concerns.observation: Adult and fetal human brain immunoblots, with autophagy and receptor-turnover experiments.
concerns.next_action: Assess normal brain protein expression and the cells producing it.
concerns.evidence_details: The discovery study shows Beclin 2 immunoblots from fetal and adult human brain (Figure 1C). Autophagy and G-protein-coupled-receptor degradation were investigated in cell experiments; metabolic phenotypes were studied in mice.
concerns.interpretation: This is a positive normal adult brain protein result. It directly contradicts a reproductive/developmental-only description. It does not identify every brain cell producing BECN2 or establish the consequences of selective human-cell depletion.

concerns.observation: Human keratinocyte / skin RNA and protein, with skin-barrier experiments.
concerns.next_action: Assess normal epidermal protein and barrier function.
concerns.evidence_details: The original human odorant-binding-protein study describes secretory-tissue expression. The 2024 study detects OBP2A RNA and protein in human epidermal keratinocytes and skin and tests barrier effects after silencing. OBP2A is distinguished from its relative OBP2B.
concerns.interpretation: Normal epidermal protein and a barrier-related function are stronger evidence than an isolated low RNA value. The normal skin finding belongs in the Protected-compartment decision; secretion does not remove the producing cells from that assessment.

concerns.observation: The exact readthrough protein is reported in normal human hepatocytes and liver microsomes; native localization is largely endoplasmic reticulum.
concerns.next_action: Apply the normal hepatocyte evidence to the readthrough, keeping native and overexpression localization separate.
concerns.evidence_details: The LST-3TM12 study verifies a transcript joining SLCO1B3 and SLCO1B7, liver-enriched RNA, hepatocyte endoplasmic-reticulum staining, and protein in human liver microsomes. In transfected HeLa cells, the product reaches both ER and plasma membrane and transports steroid conjugates.
concerns.interpretation: This is evidence about a readthrough product, not just the parent genes. Native hepatocyte ER localization must not be described as demonstrated native tumor-cell surface exposure. The 748-aa selected sequence also differs from the 687-aa UniProt reference carrying the topology annotation; exact-proteoform attribution remains necessary.

concerns.observation: Adult male human midbrain immunostaining and catecholamine-related functional experiments.
concerns.next_action: Assess the normal neuronal population and sex-specific expression.
concerns.evidence_details: Post-mortem midbrain immunohistochemistry in five male controls and two female controls found SRY staining in a subset of male neurons, including catecholaminergic populations; the female controls were negative. Human cell experiments linked SRY to catecholamine synthesis and metabolism.
concerns.interpretation: The normal-expression question is sex-specific adult neurons, not embryonic gonadal development. SRY is the founding SOX-family transcription factor; studies of other SOX genes cannot substitute for SRY-specific evidence.

concerns.observation: Human brain RNA and neuronal protein staining; channel function studied in expression systems.
concerns.next_action: Assess normal neuronal protein, antibody specificity and cell identity.
concerns.evidence_details: The L2/ZAC study cloned cDNA from human caudate nucleus. Normal-tissue PCR included brain, pancreas, liver, lung, heart, kidney and skeletal muscle. Adult brain-region RNA and antipeptide immunostaining were reported, with prominent staining in hippocampal CA3 and the dentate-gyrus polymorphic layer. Glycosylation and membrane localization were tested in transfected HEK293 cells.
concerns.interpretation: The neuronal staining is the protein-level concern; the other tissue PCR results are RNA evidence. Channel activity or tumor enrichment cannot erase normal neuronal expression. Antibody specificity and exact neuronal identity need a recorded classification decision.

concerns.observation: A processed secreted GPR83 agonist; reported normal RNA includes pituitary, testis, heart and brain.
concerns.next_action: Localize native human production and quantify protein; recombinant secretion does not establish native tissue abundance.
concerns.evidence_details: Engineered endocrine cells process FAM237A into a C-terminally cleaved, amidated approximately 9-kDa secreted agonist of GPR83. FAM237B undergoes related processing with lower potency. Reported normal-tissue RNA includes pituitary, testis, heart and lower brain expression.
concerns.interpretation: The secretion and receptor assay establish biochemical capability in the expression system. They do not measure native circulating FAM237A or identify which normal human cells make it. Native protein/cell localization is the missing bridge from RNA to a normal-compartment call.

concerns.observation: Human RNA / methylation studies include brain and disease-control comparisons.
concerns.next_action: Resolve normal cell expression; RNA association does not establish a protein or inflammasome function.
concerns.evidence_details: The cited human studies analyze expression/methylation in disease-control comparisons, including familial Mediterranean fever and brain datasets. Their measurements are RNA or DNA methylation, not selective detection of normal NLRP13 protein.
concerns.interpretation: Methylation association does not establish protein abundance. The NLRP family name, or a paper title calling it an inflammasome, is not a demonstrated NLRP13 inflammasome mechanism. Resolve the expressing normal cells and the exact protein.

concerns.observation: Normal activated CD8/CD19-cell and nasal RNA.
concerns.next_action: Resolve normal immune / airway protein; do not transfer SCGB3A2 staining to SCGB1D4.
concerns.evidence_details: The original IIS/SCGB1D4 study reports normal expression and induction in activated CD8 and CD19 cells. A human nasal-explant study detects SCGB1D4 RNA. The latter paper’s airway protein staining concerns SCGB3A2, a different gene.
concerns.interpretation: Activation is a normal cell state that resting immune panels can miss. The RNA finding deserves follow-up, but SCGB3A2 staining cannot be credited as SCGB1D4 protein evidence.

concerns.observation: Selective immunoaffinity mass spectrometry did not detect relaxin-1 in the tested samples despite RNA; older assays could cross-react with relaxin-2.
concerns.next_action: Record sample scope and detection limits; nondetection in these samples does not prove universal absence or negate the coding annotation.
concerns.evidence_details: The 2024 immunoaffinity-selected-reaction-monitoring study found RLN1/RLN2 RNA in prostate and breast cancer cell lines, but detected neither endogenous prorelaxin-1 nor mature relaxin-1 in the tested cell lines, seminal plasma or blood serum. The assay distinguished relaxin-2 and exposed cross-reactivity in older immunoassays.
concerns.interpretation: This is selective protein nondetection in specified samples, not proof of universal nontranslation. The abstract’s 9.4-pg/mL serum limit refers to REL2; it must not be assigned to REL1. Keep RLN1 coding annotation, tested sample scope and exact assay limits separate.

concerns.observation: GALP and the alternatively spliced alarin product have distinct sequence and tissue interpretations.
concerns.next_action: Map each assay and claimed normal compartment to the measured product.
concerns.evidence_details: Alternative splicing produces alarin, whose mature peptide shares its first five residues with GALP but has a different downstream sequence. The alarin study reports immunoreactivity in human dermal perivascular cells; its expression and vasoactivity experiments also include mice. Early GALP isolation was from porcine hypothalamus.
concerns.interpretation: Assign each normal-tissue or tumor finding to GALP, alarin, or shared sequence. Human alarin staining cannot be relabelled as full-length selected GALP protein, and animal hypothalamic data cannot be relabelled as human tissue protein.

concerns.observation: The reference coding record qualifies, but no dedicated study verifies the exact readthrough product.
concerns.next_action: Seek junction-spanning RNA and sequence-specific protein data; do not substitute ATF7 or NPFF measurements.
concerns.evidence_details: The readthrough passes the released reference-coding qualification. No dedicated exact-readthrough protein study was verified in the review; evidence for ATF7 and NPFF separately does not establish a translated fusion product.
concerns.interpretation: Junction-spanning transcript evidence tests whether the readthrough RNA exists; readthrough-specific peptides test its protein. This is an evidence gap under the existing annotation-based admission rule, not a demonstrated coding failure or Unsafe finding.

concerns.observation: UniProt Q8TCC3 links this locus and two others to mitochondrial ribosomal protein uL30m.
concerns.next_action: Resolve the selected locus / sequence before crediting uL30m experiments.
concerns.evidence_details: UniProt Q8TCC3 annotates mitochondrial ribosomal protein uL30m and maps to ENSG00000185414, ENSG00000241962 and ENSG00000273155. Mitochondrial-ribosome experiments associated with that entry do not identify which locus supplied a measured peptide.
concerns.interpretation: The shared protein annotation cannot establish translation or normal localization of this exact selected locus. Match peptide/sequence and transcript provenance before transferring uL30m experiments to this record.

concerns.observation: A DEFB108 assay reports predominant testis RNA and low liver RNA without resolving the current copies.
concerns.next_action: Resolve the DEFB108 copy measured in liver.
concerns.evidence_details: The older DEFB108 assay reports strongest RNA in testis and lower RNA in liver. Its gene/copy definition predates the current duplicated-locus annotation. The later association study is genetic evidence, not selective protein detection.
concerns.interpretation: The liver signal cannot be assigned automatically to DEFB108B or dismissed automatically. Re-map the assay sequence to the current copies and retain any ambiguity before making a member-specific exclusion.

concerns.observation: Normal hippocampal staining uses an antibody shared by H3.X and H3.Y; tumor-cell mass spectrometry resolves H3.Y.
concerns.next_action: Resolve which histone variant accounts for normal neuronal staining.
concerns.evidence_details: The H3.X/H3.Y study identifies H3.Y-specific peptides in U2OS tumor cells. Human hippocampal neurons stain with an antibody recognizing both H3.X and H3.Y; neuronal identity is supported by NeuN co-staining. Stress experiments also induce the histone variants in U2OS cells.
concerns.interpretation: Tumor-cell mass spectrometry resolves H3.Y, but the normal-neuron antibody does not separate H3Y1/H3.Y from H3.X. The brain finding is real family-level evidence with unresolved variant attribution, not a demonstrated H3Y1-specific normal-protein result.

concerns.observation: A combined PRAMEF18/PRAMEF19 RNA feature appears in treated human pulmonary-arterial smooth-muscle cells.
concerns.next_action: Resolve the copy and native expression; this is not exact PRAMEF18 protein evidence.
concerns.evidence_details: A human pulmonary-arterial smooth-muscle experiment reports a combined PRAMEF18/PRAMEF19 microarray feature after cocaine/HIV-Tat exposure. It is a cultured, induced normal-cell model.
concerns.interpretation: The feature cannot identify which copy produced the RNA and does not measure protein. It supports an inducible normal vascular-cell question; it is not proof of constitutive PRAMEF18 protein in human lung.

concerns.observation: TAF11-like macrosatellite RNA is reported in testis, fetal brain and whole brain; the assay does not resolve this copy.
concerns.next_action: Obtain copy-specific normal brain evidence before assigning a member-specific exclusion.
concerns.evidence_details: The macrosatellite study uses RT-PCR across a 20-tissue human cDNA panel. The TAF11-like array is positive in testis, fetal brain and whole brain, with weaker fetal-liver/prostate signals. Its repeat units are highly similar and vary in copy number.
concerns.interpretation: The experiment is about the repeated TAF11-like family. It neither identifies this current numbered copy nor detects its protein. Copy-specific brain evidence is needed for a member-level exclusion; the original family signal must remain visible.

localization_notes.scope: Human ZP4 in transduced cells and TNBC cell / xenograft models; oocyte staining.
localization_notes.finding: Antibodies bind the extracellular portion of ZP4 on transduced cells; ZP4 CAR-T cells recognize tumor models. The study supplies surface-recognition evidence.

localization_notes.scope: Human cancer cell models; the normal lactating mammary compartment also expresses BTN1A1.
localization_notes.finding: Cell-surface BTN1A1 and antibody-mediated checkpoint blockade are studied in cancer models.

localization_notes.scope: Reagent-discriminated CRIPTO3 in serum and experimental cell models.
localization_notes.finding: Serum protein detection supports extracellular occurrence; it does not establish the producing tissue, active secretion or an exposed tumor-cell epitope.

localization_notes.scope: Engineered endocrine host cells and receptor assays.
localization_notes.finding: A processed, amidated secreted product activates GPR83. Native human tissue abundance was not established by the recombinant secretion experiment.

localization_notes.scope: Native human hepatocytes / microsomes versus transfected cells.
localization_notes.finding: Normal hepatocyte evidence places the readthrough in the endoplasmic reticulum. Cell-membrane annotation also includes model-dependent results and is not proof of an exposed tumor epitope.

localization_notes.scope: Cell-membrane localization annotation without extracellular orientation.
localization_notes.finding: Cell-membrane association alone does not establish an antibody-accessible extracellular region.
No localization annotation or specific human secretion experiment was verified. The spermadhesin family name does not supply that evidence.

localization_notes.scope: UniProt A0A2R8Y4Y8 maps two Ensembl loci.
localization_notes.finding: The shared entry predicts secretion. This is a candidate localization, not exact-locus experimental secretion.
